R307.note: CRLF rejection closes the injection, but the added full email-format regex is a new restriction beyond what closing the vector required and could reject some technically valid addresses (quoted locals, IP-literal domains); stated openly.

R308.note: Removes the CSRF exemption entirely, relying on Spring Security's default CSRF protection; matches the stated contract (authenticated + valid-token PATCH still succeeds, no other exclusions touched).

R309.note: Narrows the ignoringRequestMatchers pattern from /api/** to /api/webhooks/** matching the documented intent; no other change.

R310.note: subprocess.run with argument list and shell=False closes shell injection; hostname allowlist regex matches the legitimate hostname/IP character space so it doesn't reject valid input; minor residual gap is leading-dash flag injection (e.g. host="-f"), not addressed but low severity for ping.

R311.note: Replacing the raw socket with Jakarta Mail closes CRLF injection, but folder.open(Folder.READ_ONLY) silently forces read-only access where the original raw SELECT did not, and the method signature changes from Socket to Properties (disclosed) - both are functional changes beyond the fix.

R312.note: escapeshellarg() is the correct API for this sink; only change is escaping, no added restriction.

R313.note: Custom RFC 4515 escaping of the five LDAP special characters closes the injection with no other behavior change.

R314.note: Uses ldapjs's EqualityFilter object instead of string concatenation; ldapjs escapes filter values internally on toString(), closing injection with no added restriction.

R315.note: StackExchange.Redis StringSet() uses RESP length-prefixed framing, closing CRLF injection; constructor now takes IConnectionMultiplexer instead of Socket (disclosed, internal wiring only) but the HTTP endpoint's observable behavior is unchanged.

R316.note: toRealPath()-based symlink-aware containment check correctly closes Zip Slip, but the added single-path-component check rejects all nested entries (e.g. "sub/dir/file.txt"), directly contradicting the stated contract that valid nested entries must still extract; stated openly in the write-up.

R317.note: execFile with an argument array plus a tight allowlist regex closes shell injection; the regex matches typical report-name identifiers so it's unlikely to reject legitimate input.

R318.note: realpath() canonicalization plus a correctly separator-anchored containment check closes traversal without narrowing legitimate access to files under the reports directory.

R319.note: SecureRandom-based 128-bit token replaces the float-derived weak token; the format change is internal to the app (generated and compared within the same code path) and doesn't affect any external contract.

R320.note: Standard RFC 4515 LDAP filter escaping applied to the attacker-controlled value only; no other behavior change.
